decisions.statement: A refresh runs no check.
The index is brought level with the repository as the repository is.
The commit the report names is read from HEAD as the repair opens.
The index is repaired in place.
The index is repaired file by file.
The landing lock is held from reading HEAD to the last file written.
A flag belonging to a command that writes is refused rather than ignored.
`--plan` says the change the repair would make, writing no file and making no commit.
An entry that would not file is refused.
A refresh takes away every path under the index that no entry names.
The report names the files the index differed in as well as counting the files.
The report counts the files under each index the difference falls in.
A refresh commits what git holds of the files that refresh wrote.
A refresh commits no file git ignores.
A refresh that wrote nothing git holds makes no commit.
That commit is made under the landing lock the repair is held by.
A body a hand is still writing is taken as the body stands.
A refresh that stopped part way is refused naming each index it wrote into and how many files.
That refusal names the file the refresh had in hand when the refresh stopped.
A refresh that stopped before it wrote an index file says the index is as it was.
Every answer here is built by a function rather than written out as a value.
A root holding no domain page is a fault of the data.
An entry that would not file is a fault of the data.
A commit that would not be read is an operational fault.
A refresh that stopped part way is an operational fault.

definition: the command repairing the index against the pages the repository has
